messages:
priya: quick FYI — I ran into inconsistent client-facing errors while testing the new routing fallback. sometimes we return 503 + generic body, sometimes 429 with quota info. UX/SDK folks: this is confusing for customers and makes retry heuristics messy.

priya: example responses I saw: 
priya: `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable`
priya: ```json
{
  "error": "service_unavailable",
  "message": "temporarily overloaded"
}
```

priya: and then later for same flow: 
priya: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
priya: ```json
{
  "error": "rate_limit",
  "quota_left": 0,
  "retry_after_ms": 1200
}
```

dan: ugh, yep. that's from routing choosing fallback (503) vs quota enforcement (429). we haven't standardized when to include usable hints like `retry_after_ms` or `quota_id`.
dan: proposal: canonicalize into two orthogonal axes in the payload: transport status and machine-readable problem_code. e.g. status 503 still possible, but body should include `problem_code: \"quota_exhausted\"` or `problem_code: \"routing_overload\"` so SDKs can make consistent decisions.

alex: +1 on the problem_code idea. also add `client_hint` with enum values (RETRY, FALLBACK, CONTACT_SUPPORT). that keeps user-visible message short but actionable.

marco: small concern: customers expect 429 for throttling (and they already parse it). if we keep returning 503 sometimes they'll have to change logic. can we map both to 429 when it's truly a quota/rlim issue? reserve 503 for infra-level outages only.

priya: agreed on mapping. routing fallback should only produce 503 when the downstream model instance is unhealthy or region is down. if fallback is due to capacity tiering then prefer 429 with `fallback_policy: \"degraded\"` in body.

dan: question for ops: ops-bot, what telemetry do we currently attach to 503 vs 429? any strong reason to keep different codes?

ops-bot: automation note — current routing telemetry tags: `http_status`, `route_fallback`, `quota_check`. 503s are being tagged as `route_fallback:true` and are NOT currently annotated with `quota_id` or `retry_after_ms`. 429s include `quota_id` & `retry_after_ms` in logs.

alex: ok so action items: (1) SDK-friendly canonical error schema, (2) policy: when to use 429 vs 503, (3) console surface: show quota hint + direct link to quota buy/appeal when `quota_id` present.

priya: draft schema suggestion (very small): 
priya: ```json
{
  "http_status": 429,
  "problem_code": "quota_limit_exceeded",
  "client_hint": "RETRY_AFTER",
  "retry_after_ms": 1500,
  "quota_id": "team-1234-ingress",
  "ui_link": "https://console.redwood.ai/account/quota/team-1234"
}
```

dan: love the `ui_link` idea for console integration. console team — that lets you show a CTA right in the error diagnostics panel and tie into rollouts.

marco: for rollouts, we should also include `rollout_policy_version` and `served_variant` so that we can A/B measure error rates by variant without extra tracing.

priya: good call. append those to schema. also include `fallback_path` enum to clarify whether request was routed to lower-tier model, different region, or queue.

ops-bot: note — adding fields will increase payload size. we should make fields opt-in via a `client_accepts_v2_errors` request header so older SDKs keep current compact payloads. telemetry will record whether `client_accepts_v2_errors` was present.

alex: implement plan: 
alex: - eng-platform: spec `error-v2` and mapping table for http_status vs problem_code (owner: dan)
alex: - eng-runtime: annotate routing decisions with `problem_code` and `served_variant` (owner: marco)
alex: - devex/SDK: parse problem_code & client_hint, fallback to status-based heuristics if header absent (owner: alex)
alex: - console: render CTA when `ui_link` present and aggregate counts by `problem_code` (owner: priya)

priya: timeline? can we do a short PR for the spec by EOD Friday? stakeholders: SRE, runtime, SDK, console.

dan: I can draft the mapping table and PR by Thu. marco will add runtime instrumentation.

marco: will prototype instrumentation changes next week. ops-bot: please add an alert rule to watch for a spike in 503s that do NOT include `problem_code` — that should fail our rollout gating.

ops-bot: alert created: `503_missing_problem_code_spike` -> notifications to #eng-oncall and #eng-platform. threshold: +200% over baseline for 5m.

priya: awesome. last note: update docs & changelog. we should call this `error-v2` and include migration guidance for customers (how to opt-in & a deprecation plan for the mixed behavior).

alex: also add a short example in SDK README with recommended retry/backoff logic using `client_hint` and `retry_after_ms`.

priya: thanks all. I'll post the spec PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:
